@graph.headline: The Most Common Token Launch PR Mistakes in 2026
@graph.alternativeHeadline: TGE PR pitfalls and fixes: no news hook, hype without proof, APAC gaps, KOL fraud, and post-launch silence
@graph.description: The avoidable errors that quietly sink a TGE in 2026: no real news hook, hype copy with no proof, ignoring APAC media markets, buying KOLs without vetting follower quality, missing compliance review, and going silent after the token goes live. Includes the fix for each mistake and a clean TGE PR timeline.

itemListElement.name: The Most Common Token Launch PR Mistakes in 2026

mainEntity.name: What is the biggest token launch PR mistake in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common and costly mistake is pitching an announcement with no real news hook. 'We are launching our token' is not news. A named raise figure, a mainnet milestone with a verifiable usage number, or a named partnership that changes what your product can do: these are news. If you cannot answer 'why is this news today and not six months from now?' in one sentence with a number or a name, you are not ready to pitch. Build the hook before you build the release.

mainEntity.name: How do you vet KOLs for a token launch campaign?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for three things before committing any budget: recent analytics showing impressions and reach on organic posts, at least one verifiable example of a past promotion that generated traceable on-chain activity, and a full list of projects they have promoted in the last ninety days. Follower count is nearly useless in isolation. Engagement rate on organic posts, geographic distribution of followers, and evidence of real conversion are what matter. Mid-tier KOLs charging $10,000 to $30,000 per post can easily have 60 to 80 percent bot followers, so looking before you pay is non-negotiable.

mainEntity.name: Why does post-launch silence hurt a token project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because in a market where attention moves fast and bad news travels faster, a two-week gap in your narrative is a vacuum that speculation fills. The first ninety days after TGE are when the community tests whether the team is real, when exchanges form their first impression of your communications, and when early holders decide whether they trust the roadmap. A structured post-launch content cadence, with milestone announcements, data updates, and founder content, is what converts launch attention into sustained credibility.

mainEntity.name: Do token launch press releases need a compliance review?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and this applies to every piece of launch copy: press releases, pitch emails, KOL briefs, and social posts. Any language that makes explicit or implied forward-looking claims about token price or investment returns is a potential securities law violation in the US and many other jurisdictions. The rule is simple: describe what the token does and what the protocol has achieved; do not predict what the token will be worth or what returns holders will see. Have legal counsel familiar with crypto securities law review everything before it publishes.

mainEntity.name: How early should token launch PR start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Narrative infrastructure should start three to six months before the TGE. By six weeks out, you should already have at least three pieces of media coverage on record, a founder op-ed placed or in progress, warm relationships with journalists on your media list, and a clear one-sentence narrative every team member says consistently. Projects that start two weeks before TGE are not doing launch PR, they are doing damage limitation.
